RagShortTexts: Henry II was defeated and killed near Legnica by Mongol forces in 1241.
Silesian houses lost a ruler, while returning fighters and refugees carried different memories.

Variants.Content: In 1241 Duke Henry II of Silesia met Mongol forces near Legnica, suffered defeat and died. His household faced succession and the reassembly of followers; towns along the roads received defeated men and displaced families. Some remember a relative lost there, while others heard the duke’s name only from travellers. Distant retellings mix observation and rumour, giving listeners reason to ask a messenger’s route and departure time.

Henry’s death required new arrangements for lands and followers. Lords discussing Legnica consider whether neighbouring princes can defend together and who will perform promises after the man who made them is gone.

A returning fighter remembers companions, mounts and a place to regroup. He may not know how every contingent scattered, but can teach recruits how he found his way home after losing sight of his banner.

Bereaved households lost labour while newcomers required food and shelter. Villagers ask about harvest, working animals and missing relatives. A duke’s funeral does not provide each family with winter grain.
